questions.question: What is diffusion?
choices: Movement of particles only against a concentration gradient
Movement of water only through a protein pump
Net movement of particles from higher to lower concentration
Transport of large particles by membrane vesicles

questions.question: What is osmosis?
choices: Net movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane
Protein production inside a ribosome
Movement of oxygen through a cell wall
Movement of ions using ATP

questions.question: Which process requires cellular energy to move a substance against its concentration gradient?
choices: Simple diffusion
Osmosis
Facilitated diffusion
Active transport

questions.question: What does homeostasis mean?
choices: Keeping all internal quantities permanently unchanged
Maintaining internal conditions within suitable ranges
Stopping exchange with the environment
Eliminating responses to external change

questions.question: Which process uses membrane proteins without directly requiring cellular energy to move substances down a gradient?
choices: Active transport
Endocytosis
Protein synthesis
Facilitated diffusion

questions.question: What is endocytosis?
choices: Release of material when a vesicle joins the membrane
Diffusion of water through a membrane
Intake of material by enclosing it in a membrane vesicle
Movement of DNA into a ribosome

questions.question: What is exocytosis?
choices: Splitting one cell into two cells
Release of vesicle contents when the vesicle fuses with the membrane
Transport of ions through a channel
Movement of water into a vacuole

questions.question: Why can oxygen enter a cell by diffusion when its concentration is higher outside?
choices: Random movement produces net movement down the concentration gradient
The cell must actively pump all oxygen inward
Oxygen is too large to cross any membrane
Diffusion occurs only when concentrations are equal

questions.question: What happens at dynamic equilibrium during diffusion?
choices: Every particle stops moving
Particles keep moving, but there is no net concentration change
All particles collect on one side
The membrane begins pumping every particle uphill

questions.question: Why can transport proteins be important for charged ions?
choices: Ions dissolve easily in the membrane's oily interior
All ions are larger than entire cells
Ions cannot move in water
The membrane's lipid interior limits their direct passage

questions.question: An animal cell is placed in a solution with a higher concentration of nonpenetrating solutes than its cytoplasm. What is expected?
choices: Water leaves and the cell shrinks
No water moves through the membrane
The cell immediately makes a cell wall
Water enters and the cell swells

questions.question: Why does a plant cell usually resist bursting when water enters?
choices: Its membrane does not permit water movement
Its nucleus pumps all water back out
Its cell wall limits expansion
Its chloroplasts remove the water

questions.question: How does negative feedback help maintain homeostasis?
choices: A response counteracts a departure from a suitable range
A response amplifies every departure from normal
It prevents an organism from detecting changes
It requires internal conditions to match the environment

questions.question: Why does sweating help cool the body?
choices: Sweat prevents any transfer of energy
Evaporation transfers energy away from the skin
Sweat increases the body's production of heat
Sweat turns body heat into stored nutrients

questions.question: Why might a cell use active transport even when diffusion is possible for other substances?
choices: Every substance moves naturally toward higher concentration
Active transport never uses proteins
The cell may need to maintain a concentration difference
Diffusion and active transport serve identical directions in every case

questions.question: Two sides of a membrane have equal initial pressure. Water can cross, but sugar cannot. One side has more dissolved sugar. Where is the initial net water movement?
choices: Toward the side with less sugar
Toward the side with less water regardless of its sugar concentration
No net movement because sugar cannot cross
Toward the side with more sugar

questions.question: A cell's ion pump stops when its ATP supply is depleted. What does this suggest about the pump?
choices: It is part of the cell wall
It performs only simple diffusion
It performs energy-dependent transport
It functions without a concentration gradient

questions.question: Body temperature rises, and a control system increases sweating. Which process does this illustrate?
choices: Negative feedback responding to a temperature change
A feedforward response before any temperature change
Positive feedback amplifying a temperature change
A fixed response unrelated to temperature

questions.question: A potato strip loses mass in a concentrated salt solution. What is the best explanation?
choices: Salt drew water into the cells until they burst
Water moved out of its cells by osmosis
Water entered the cells by active transport
Salt prevented all water movement across membranes

questions.question: A substance crosses through a membrane channel from high to low concentration without ATP. Which label fits best?
choices: Endocytosis
Exocytosis
Active transport
Facilitated diffusion
